content.user_title: Build Unity UI Toolkit Layouts and Interactions
content.value_statement: Unity UI Toolkit development requires careful handling of UXML structure, USS restrictions, and runtime interactions. This skill guides focused edits and generates layouts, custom visuals, and requested C# behavior using documented project patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explain existing UXML element hierarchies and make targeted markup or stylesheet changes.
Generate paired UXML and USS files with flexible layouts and project naming conventions.
Guide UIDocument and PanelSettings setup with project-local asset references.
Generate requested pointer interaction patterns with drag feedback and drop target validation.
Create custom VisualElement patterns and Painter2D visuals for gradients, shapes, and progress rings.
Provide runtime data binding patterns with property paths, binding modes, lifecycle cleanup, and version-specific PanelRenderer guidance.
limitations: The skill provides Markdown guidance and examples, not a standalone UI generator or bundled validation tool.
Unity import validation, Console feedback, and visual inspection require the Unity Editor and user participation.
Custom element examples target Unity 6+, while SVG and PanelRenderer guidance specify later Unity versions.
Visual screen requests default to UXML and USS; C# behavior and data bindings require explicit requests.

use_cases.title: Create a Game Menu
use_cases.description: Generate a flexible menu with UXML, USS, existing project assets, and PanelSettings setup guidance.

use_cases.title: Refine an Existing Interface
use_cases.description: Adjust colors, spacing, text wrapping, and hover states without rewriting unrelated UI elements.

use_cases.title: Connect Interactive Game Interfaces
use_cases.description: Add requested inventory drag interactions or connect health and score displays to local game data.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a UI Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the element hierarchy in [UXML file]. Identify its linked stylesheets and named elements without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand an existing UI Toolkit screen.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Focused Style Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [USS file] so [button class] uses [color] and its label wraps. Preserve unrelated selectors and existing project conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: make a narrow styling edit.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Flexible Menu
prompt_templates.prompt: Create UXML and USS for [menu description] in [feature folder]. Reuse project styles and icons, use flexible layouts, and describe required PanelSettings setup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a new runtime UI screen.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bound Inventory Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: For Unity [version], create [inventory screen] with UXML, USS, and C#. Add PointerManipulator dragging, validate equipment drops, and bind quantity labels to [data model].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine UI generation, pointer interactions, and runtime bindings.

output_examples.input: Explain my inventory UXML without changing it.
output: The root container holds a header, item grid, and details panel.
The item grid uses reusable slot elements, while the details panel contains labels for the selected item.
The explanation identifies linked stylesheets and named controls for later edits.

output_examples.input: Create a settings menu with UXML and USS only.
output: A settings document and stylesheet with a flexible control layout and shared project styling.
Existing project icons are reused where available.
Setup notes identify the required PanelSettings assignment and Unity Editor import checks.
No C# controller is included because runtime logic was not requested.

output_examples.input: Add drag behavior to my equipment slots with C#.
output: A pointer manipulator pattern handles drag start, movement, completion, and pointer release.
Valid equipment slots receive visual feedback, and invalid drops return the item to its starting position.
Item data remains separate from visual elements, and drop validation occurs before the equipment state changes.

best_practices: Provide the Unity version, relevant UI files, target folder, and explicit requirements for C# behavior or bindings.
Reuse existing project styles, assets, and naming conventions before introducing new UI resources.
Import completed changes in Unity, inspect Console messages, and verify layout and interaction states visually.
anti_patterns: Treating USS as full browser CSS without checking Unity property and selector support.
Requesting broad UI rewrites for small styling changes or replacing shared assets without checking existing resources.
Assuming a visual inventory screen includes drag behavior or accepting generated files without Unity Editor checks.

faq.question: What does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers Unity UI Toolkit UXML, USS, custom elements, pointer interactions, Painter2D visuals, and runtime data binding patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. File editing and Unity integration depend on the available host tools.

faq.question: Does it validate generated UI automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled validator is provided. The workflow relies on Unity Editor import feedback, Console messages, and visual checks.

faq.question: Will a menu request generate C# scripts?
faq.answer: Menu and screen requests default to UXML and USS. Request functional logic, pointer behavior, or runtime bindings explicitly when C# is needed.

faq.question: Does it support every Unity version?
faq.answer: Examples include Unity 6+ custom elements, Unity 6.3+ SVG guidance, and Unity 6.6+ PanelRenderer guidance. Confirm API availability in your version.

faq.question: Can it use existing project assets?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the assistant to search for existing styles, icons, and PanelSettings, then reuse appropriate project resources.
